judge.notes: Structurally the code is a faithful realization of the control flow: all 5 declared relationships and all 6 elements are present, the branching order (validate -> store -> screen -> price/notify) matches the stub exactly, and all three explicit failure paths (invalid request, store unavailable, screening unavailable) are implemented with correct downstream consequences (no screening/pricing/notification on store failure; pricing+hold-but-no-notify on screening outage; notify-but-no-price on refusal; no price/notify on review). Fire-and-forget notification semantics (DT-S note 4) are preserved. However the code invents a large amount of concrete domain logic that the specification deliberately left abstract or deferred to an unseen decision table: the tariff pricing formula, the DT-V validation bounds, and the DT-S numeric risk thresholds are all fabricated constants with no spec backing. Most seriously, ScreeningService is redefined around an invented string-status-to-riskIndex mapping that has no counterpart anywhere in the spec, and the handle() wrapper adds an invented shipper-existence check and an invented mid-flow store-failure branch on update_quote. Technology annotations (FastAPI, PostgreSQL, SQL/TCP, REST/HTTPS, JSON/HTTPS) are entirely unaddressed — the code is plain in-memory Python with no framework, HTTP, or persistence trace. These inventions and the complete absence of technology fidelity substantially lower the score despite excellent flow/guard fidelity.
